questions.q: What does checking "Run scripts" on a UI Policy actually unlock?
options: A new table, sys_ui_policy_script, separate from sys_ui_policy
Two new script fields on the UI Policy itself — Execute if true and Execute if false
The ability to delete the policy's UI Policy Actions automatically
A way to run server-side GlideRecord queries from the condition builder
questions.explain: Run scripts exposes Execute if true / Execute if false directly on the UI Policy record, in addition to any declarative UI Policy Actions.

options: Access current and previous, the same way a Business Rule does
Run a GlideRecord query against the database directly
Modify a Business Rule's condition at runtime
Call any g_form method, such as setMandatory or showFieldMsg, exactly as a Client Script would
questions.explain: g_form is the same client-side form API used in Client Scripts — current/previous belong to server-side Business Rules, not this client-side function.

questions.q: A UI Policy's Run-scripts pair is best used for which real scenario?
options: Replacing Business Rules entirely for all server-side validation
A small, specific side effect (a warning message, a value reset) that should fire at the exact moment a condition the policy already evaluates becomes true
Enforcing a mandatory field no matter how the record is created, including via REST integrations
Running scheduled, time-based logic unrelated to any form field
questions.explain: The script pair layers extra client-side behavior onto a condition the UI Policy is already evaluating — it doesn't add server-side enforcement.

questions.q: A UI Policy has Run scripts checked with a working onCondition_true function. A scheduled Import Set loads 500 new Incident records overnight. What happens to onCondition_true for those records?
options: It runs, but only the UI Policy Actions are skipped
It runs once per imported record, exactly as if a user had filled out the form
It never runs, because the Import Set never renders the form in a browser
It runs only for the first record in the import batch
questions.explain: Like all UI Policy behavior, Run-scripts functions are client-side and only fire when the form actually renders in a browser — an Import Set never does that.

questions.q: What is the second argument passed into both onCondition_true and onCondition_false, and where else has this course already used it?
options: current — the same server-side record object introduced in Chapter 1's Business Rules
g_form — the same client-side form API introduced in Chapter 2's Client Scripts
previous — the prior state of the record before the condition changed
g_form — but it behaves completely differently here than in a Client Script
questions.explain: Both functions receive control and g_form, and g_form here is identical to the g_form object Chapter 2 already covered for onLoad/onChange Client Scripts.
